senses.gloss: ch. same (with אַפִּין) to show a bright face, be pleasant; to favor (with ב or ל).
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 4:4">Targ. Y. Gen. IV, 4</cite>, sq.
Targ. Job XXXII, 22 יִסְבַּר Ms. (ed. יְסוֹבַר Poël; some ed. יְסַבַּר Pa.).—Part. pass. סָבִיר; סְבִיר אפין looked up to with favor, honored, popular. Ib. XXII, 8.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 19:32">Targ. O. Lev. XIX, 32</cite> <cite ref="O00084"><he>סָבַר</he></cite> (Y.
<cite ref="Onkelos Leviticus 19:32">ib.</cite> <he>סְבִירִין</he>).

senses.gloss: to look out for, hope; to speculate, plan; to imagine, believe.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Hosea 12:7">Targ. Hos. XII, 7</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 27:14">Targ. Ps. XXVII, 14</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 10:11">Targ. Y. Ex. X, 11</cite> <he>סַבְרִין</he>.
Targ. Prov. XIV, 12; a. fr.—Part. pass. סָבִיר, סְבִיר looking for, planning, thinking, believing.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 10:10">Targ. O. Ex. X, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 37:8">Targ. O. Gen. XXXVII, 8</cite>; a. fr.—Y. Ber. III, 6ᶜ top <he>תמן סְבִירְתֵּיה</he> there I thought about it, v. <cite ref="O00091"><he>סְבָר</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to conclude, argue, understand; to have an idea.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Samuel 12:19">Targ. II Sam. XII, 19</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 65a">B. Bath. 65ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>סָבוּר מינה וכ׳</he> they concluded from this that …, but it is not so.
<cite ref="Gittin 56a:4">Gitt. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>סבור רבנן לקרוביה</he> the scholars proposed to offer it up on the altar.
<cite ref="Ketubot 87b:12">Keth. 87ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ס׳ … למימר וכ׳</he> R … had an idea to say &c. (but was refuted).
<cite ref="Berakhot 3a">Ber. 3ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מאי קס׳ וכ׳</he> what is R. E.’s opinion? <he>אי קס׳ שלש וכ׳</he> if he holds that the night contains three watches &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 4b:10">Ib. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>ר׳ יוחנן ס׳ וכ׳</he> R. J. argues (thus) &c.
<cite ref="Berakhot 27a:4">Ib. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>מי סַבְרַת דהאי וכ׳</he> do you think that &c.?—
<cite ref="Yevamot 72b:7">Yeb. 72ᵇ</cite> <he>תנייה … וסַבְרָהּ וכ׳</he> he learned it by heart in three days, and reasoned it out (drew the logical conclusions from it) in three months.
<cite ref="Shabbat 63a:15">Sabb. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>לִיסְבַּר</he>, v. <cite ref="C01064"><he>גְּמַר</he> II</cite>.

Keth. 77ᵃ דקסַבְרָא וקבילא for she understood well (her husband’s physical condition) and accepted it; ib. הא סְבִירָא וקבילא did she not understand and accept? B. Mets. 65ᵃ סַבְרַת וקבילת thou didst understand and accept; a. fr.—ס׳ כ to think like, to agree with, adopt the opinion of.
Succ. 33ᵇ ס׳ לה כותיה בחדא ופליג וכ׳ he agrees with him in one point, and differs in another point; a. fr.—סְבִירָא ל is of the opinion, shares the opinion.
<cite ref="Sukkah 33a:12">Ib. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>אי ס׳ לן וכ׳</he> if we accept the opinion that &c.

<cite ref="Chullin 48a:15">Ḥull. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>וליה לא ס׳ ליה</he> (abbr. <he>ל״ס</he>) but he himself does not entertain that opinion; a. fr.—Tanḥ.P’kudé 2 <he>סַבְרֵי מרנן</he> have the gentlemen formed an opinion?, i.e. how do you vote?—
<cite ref="Chullin 48a:15">Ib.</cite> (introducing the benediction over wine) <he>סברי מרנן</he> have you agreed (to allow me to say the prayer)?, i.e. with your permission!—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 32a:12">B. Kam. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>ותִסְבְּרָא</he> how can you understand that?, i.e. is this not a contradiction?—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 34:15">Gen. R. s. 34</cite>; s. 38 <he>הוה מַסְבַּר ליה ולא ס׳</he> he explained to him, but he could not comprehend; <he>מאי טעמא לית את סבר</he> why is it that you do not comprehend?
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 49:18">Targ. O. Gen. XLIX, 18</cite> <he>סַבָּרִית</he> (ed. Berl. <he>סָבַרִית</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 32:22">Targ. Job XXXII, 22</cite>, v. supra.
Targ. Prov. XI, 28 מַסְבִּיר Ed. Lag. (oth. ed. מְסַבַּר Pa.); a. e.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 22:10">Targ. Ps. XXII, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 6:26">Targ. Y. Num. VI, 26</cite> <he>יַסְבַּר סְבַר אפוי</he>.
<cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 2:55">Targ. I Chr. II, 55</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 48a:3">Ḥull. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>רבין</he> … <he>אַסְבְּרָהּ לי</he> Rabin … made it clear to me.
B. Mets. 33ᵃ דאַסְבְּרָן זוהמא וכ׳ who explained to us what zomalistron meant.

<cite ref="Eruvin 21b:22">Erub. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>ואַסְבְּרָהּ במאי דדמי ליה</he> and illustrated it by a simile. Y. ib. X, beg. 26ᵃ <he>אַסְבְּרִי רב וכ׳</he> R. H. enlightened me (saying) &c. Gen. R. l. c., v. supra; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to look for, hope; to plan, intend.
units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 106:13">Targ. Ps. CVI, 13</cite>.—
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 49:17">Targ. Y. II, Gen. XLIX, 17</cite>.

senses.gloss: to be understood, be intelligible, evident; to be rational, logical.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 31b">R. Hash. 31ᵇ</cite> sq. <he>אמר מלתא וא׳ טעמיה וכ׳</he> he said something, and his argument appeared reasonable, and his teacher instituted the usage in his (R. Joḥanan’s) name. Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40ᵃ <he>לא מִסְתַּבְּרָא כאהין סוברה וכ׳</he> it is not reasonable to follow this opinion that it is not forbidden.
<cite ref="Berakhot 36a:15">Ber. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>כותך מסתברא</he> it is reasonable to follow thy opinion, i.e. thou art obviously right.
<cite ref="Shabbat 76a:3">Sabb. 76ᵃ</cite> <he>אדרבא כדמעיקרא מס׳</he> on the contrary, that which he first said stands to reason; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (cmp. צָפַן) provide one’s self; to store up for one’s self.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 39:9">Targ. Ez. XXXIX, 9</cite>.  v. <cite ref="I00589"><he>טִסְבְּרָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="V00758"><he>תִּסְבְּרָא</he></cite>.
